evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/voice_commands.rs:248 and :278 — action_check_balance() and action_report_fault() are shipped stubs that return VoiceActionResult{ success: true } with fabricated data on a LIVE webhook path, not TODO-gated code. action_check_balance always answers 'balance is zero, no outstanding fees' (hardcoded data.balance=0.0) without querying any financial repo; action_report_fault mints a throwaway Uuid::new_v4() ticket, speaks it back to the resident ('The manager will be notified shortly'), and NEVER persists a fault row. Full call path traced reachable in production: routes/voice_webhooks.rs:146/162/265 -> VoiceCommandService::process_command -> match on intent (voice_commands.rs:143-144) -> these handlers. Failure scenario: a resident who owes fees is told they owe nothing (financial misinformation), and a spoken 'the elevator is broken' / 'gas smell' fault report is silently dropped with a confirmation number that maps to no ticket (data loss on a possibly safety-relevant path).

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/actions/api_call.rs:179 (validate_external_url) — the private/internal-IP guard only runs when the host is a LITERAL IP (`if let Ok(ip) = host.parse::<IpAddr>()`). A DNS hostname that resolves to a private/link-local/metadata IP (e.g. 169.254.169.254, 10.x, fc00::/7) is not a literal IP, is not in the small blocked_hosts denylist, and does not end in .local/.internal, so it passes validation; reqwest then resolves it at send time (validate-then-resolve TOCTOU / DNS-rebinding SSRF). The URL is not admin-static: execute() (line ~240) runs context.substitute_template(&api_config.url) over trigger data before validation. Failure scenario: a workflow api_call action with url 'http://<attacker-host>/' where <attacker-host> resolves to the cloud metadata endpoint reaches internal infra; the IPv6/IPv4-literal hardening (P1-06 comment) never fires because no literal IP is present. Fix requires resolving the host and re-checking every resolved address (or pinning the connection) rather than parsing the host string as an IP.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/workflow_executor.rs:481-486 — evaluate_conditions() fails OPEN: a condition JSON value that deserializes as neither ConditionGroup nor Condition is logged and skipped, and the function ultimately returns Ok(true). The condition set is the gate that decides whether a workflow (which can send emails, mutate data, and make outbound api_call requests — see the SSRF finding) runs. Failure scenario: schema drift or a renamed/malformed condition object silently drops the intended guard, so the workflow fires when it should have been blocked. Likelihood is low (conditions are admin-authored) but it is a concrete fail-open on a gating decision; safer to fail closed (Ok(false) / propagate an error) on an unparseable condition.
